scope: Source-controlled descriptive OOF counts; token length is not interference density or harmful span position

difference_of_gains_group_bootstrap.scope: Explored train-internal B group-OOF analysis, conditional on this fixed A-only checkpoint, split and fitted readouts. Bootstrap resamples held groups without retraining; it does not include LoRA/head fitting variance, fresh-dataset shift or full pipeline uncertainty. Formal validation/test remain unopened by this analysis.

limitations: Fixed length bins and sources are preserved; this is exploratory, not a new layer/threshold/model selection exercise.
Large length bins can be nearly entirely JailBench and JailBench is single-class harmful, so marginal long-text accuracy is source/label-confounded.
WildGuard long bins can be very sparse; small counts cannot establish a stable length effect or a mechanism.
Token length does not measure irrelevant-content fraction, harmful-span position, semantic complexity, or direct interference among hidden layers.
Short inputs can contain semantic distraction; a short length distribution does not disprove that possibility.
Pooling and multi-layer fixed-head score changes are descriptive predictive effects; fitted checkpoints, stopping and dev threshold transfer also change.
No new interference annotations, controlled distractors/positions, label repairs, training or formal holdout access occurred.
